title: Capitals of Europe
description: The capitals of the European states: where they are, what makes them special, and their position on the map.

cards.back:
Capital of Italy. It stands on the Tiber and contains Vatican City. According to tradition it was founded in 753 BC.

[mappa: Rome]

Capital of France. Crossed by the Seine, it is the city of the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.

[mappa: Paris]

Capital of Germany. On the Spree. From 1961 to 1989 it was divided by the Wall; since 1990 it has been the capital of reunified Germany.

[mappa: Berlin]

Capital of Spain. In the centre of the Iberian Peninsula, on the Manzanares river; home to the Prado Museum.

[mappa: Madrid]

Capital of Portugal. On the Tagus estuary, facing the Atlantic; it was largely destroyed by the 1755 earthquake.

[mappa: Lisbon]

Capital of Austria. On the Danube; it was the capital of the Habsburg empire and is tied to great classical music.

[mappa: Vienna]

Capital of Switzerland. On the Aare river; it is the Swiss «federal city» and its old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[mappa: Bern]

Capital of Belgium. Home to many European Union institutions, such as the Commission and the Council, and to NATO headquarters.

[mappa: Brussels]

Capital of the Netherlands. The constitutional capital, famous for its canals; the government and parliament, however, sit in The Hague.

[mappa: Amsterdam]

Capital of Poland. On the Vistula; its old town, destroyed in the Second World War, was rebuilt and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[mappa: Warsaw]

Capital of the Czech Republic. On the Vltava, with the Charles Bridge and the vast Prague Castle complex.

[mappa: Prague]

Capital of Hungary. On the Danube; it was created in 1873 by uniting Buda, Óbuda and Pest.

[mappa: Budapest]

Capital of Greece. Dominated by the Acropolis and the Parthenon, it is considered the cradle of democracy.

[mappa: Athens]

Capital of Sweden. Built on islands between Lake Mälaren and the Baltic Sea; the Nobel Prizes are awarded here, except the Peace Prize.

[mappa: Stockholm]

Capital of Norway. At the head of the Oslofjord; the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded here.

[mappa: Oslo]

Capital of Denmark. On the Øresund, facing Sweden, to which it is linked by a bridge; famous for the Little Mermaid statue.

[mappa: Copenhagen]

Capital of Finland. Facing the Gulf of Finland, in the Baltic Sea.

[mappa: Helsinki]

Capital of Ireland. At the mouth of the Liffey, on Dublin Bay.

[mappa: Dublin]

Capital of the United Kingdom. On the Thames; the British parliament and government sit in Westminster.

[mappa: London]

Capital of Slovenia. Crossed by the Ljubljanica river, with its castle on the hill in the centre.

[mappa: Ljubljana]

Capital of Croatia. On the Sava river, at the foot of Mount Medvednica.

[mappa: Zagreb]

Capital of Romania. On the Dâmbovița river; the Palace of the Parliament is among the largest buildings in the world.

[mappa: Bucharest]

Capital of Bulgaria. At the foot of Mount Vitosha, in the west of the country.

[mappa: Sofia]

Capital of Estonia. On the Gulf of Finland; its medieval old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[mappa: Tallinn]

Capital of Latvia. On the Daugava, near the Gulf of Riga; famous for its Art Nouveau buildings.

[mappa: Riga]

Capital of Lithuania. At the confluence of the Neris and Vilnia rivers; its baroque old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[mappa: Vilnius]

Capital of Slovakia. On the Danube, on the border with Austria and Hungary.

[mappa: Bratislava]

Capital of Iceland. It is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state in the world.

[mappa: Reykjavík]

Capital of Malta. Founded by the Knights of St John in 1566, it is one of the smallest capitals in the European Union.

[mappa: Valletta]

Capital of Luxembourg. Seat of the Court of Justice of the European Union; its old town, with the ancient fortifications, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

[mappa: Q1842]
